In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cofilin is a key regulator of actin cytoskeletal rearrangements in FRDA neurons.
the lack of frataxin in YG8R neurons is associated with an abnormal actin cytoskeletal structure and dynamics in axons and growth cones.
cofilin dysregulations in the absence of frataxin lead to an increase in F/G-actin ratios in the GC and the axon, which could be responsible for the lack of sensory axons and neurons in FRDA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cofilin-ARP2/3 dysregulation is a novel mechanism for the loss of neurons in FRDA.
frataxin deficiency alters actin dynamics by dysregulation of cofilin- and ARP 2/3-dependent pathways.
the dysregulation of cofilin and actin-related protein 2/3 is a consequence of the lack of frataxin in DRG neurons, and it is a possible cause for the observed decrease in neurite growth.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the loss of frataxin in DRG neurons results in the dysregulation of the actin cytoskeletal dynamics, which is likely to contribute to the loss of sensory neurons in Friedreich’s atxaia.
cofilin-ARP2/3 signalling is an important target for the development of therapies to counteract the loss of DRG neurons in FRDA.
the cofilin-ARP2/3 pathway may be a potential therapeutic target to prevent the neuronal loss in FRDA.
